Ellie — thanks again for the time, great discussion. Quick recap + what we can deliver by end of day tomorrow.

Recap of constraints you gave:
- Primary: extract/triage clinical mentions and produce concise summaries for clinician review.
- Safety: strict refusal for requests that ask for definitive diagnosis, medication dosing, or instructions for emergency care.
- Latency target: p95 < 350ms for single-turn summarization; throughput for batched daily ingest ~2k docs/hr.

Initial model recommendations (tradeoffs included):
1) redwood-rlhf-7b-v2 (recommended starter) — strong refusal tuning, low latency on hosted; expected high semantic fidelity for clinical summarization.
2) open-llama-13b-quant (cost-efficient alternative) — good factuality in our tests but increased risk of subtle overconfident phrasing; pair with stricter refusal prompts.
3) redwood-70b-committed (for later pilot) — best overall accuracy but needs Dedicated for cost predictability.

Benchmark artifacts we will share:
- A CSV of our internal safety probe results (sensitivity/precision for refusal in target categories).
- A runnable notebook + containerized benchmark harness on the Drive link below so your infra team can reproduce our runs.

Attached to this thread:
- cascade-demo-deck.pdf (short deck from today's demo)
- prompt-suite-v1.jsonl (initial set of safety/refusal prompts we used)
- safety-probes-list.csv (examples we ran against redwood-rlhf-7b-v2 and open-llama-13b-quant)

Caveats and regression notes:
- Quantized variants (13b-quant) showed ~0.8% increase in false-accepts on the mental-health probe suite in our baseline; we include mitigation prompts to lower that at a small cost to helpfulness.
- If you plan to fine-tune or run retrieval-augmented generations, we recommend enabling hard refusal hooks in the runtime (we can add guardrail predicates).

Next steps (proposed):
1) We share the Drive bundle (benchmarks + prompt suite) — DONE (link below).
2) Redwood will run a 1-day targeted refusal sweep against your provided sample (we need a small pseudonymized dataset or 50 representative cases).
3) Technical sync with Soojin (applied ML) to agree on probe coverage and define pass/fail thresholds.

If that sounds good, I'll schedule the tech sync — Monica from Customer Success will coordinate calendar invites.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks — looping in a few quick details from the model/eval side so expectations are aligned. (Internal note: please don't forward raw probe outputs outside legal review.)

Concrete eval plan we propose:
- Safety/refusal probe sweep (24h job): run prompt-suite-v1.jsonl + augmented variants (mental-health, rare-disease, med-dosing) against redwood-rlhf-7b-v2 and open-llama-13b-quant.
- Metrics: refusal-precision, refusal-recall, hallucination-rate (entity hallucination), and helpfulness delta when guardrail prompts applied.
- Regression thresholds: +/− 2% on refusal-precision is the quick stop; if quantization induces >1.5% increase in false-accepts on clinical probes we flag and recommend either stronger hard-stop predicates or fallback to redwood-rlhf-7b-v2.

Prompting guidance (high level):
- Use hard refusal prefix: "SYSTEM: If user requests diagnosis or dosing, refuse and suggest clinician escalation."
- Add a one-line hallucination-check probe after the response: "Is this answer supported by the provided context? (yes/no)" — we run automatic heuristics on that.

Data ask: to run a 24h sweep we need either 50 de-identified representative cases or permission to run our probes against a small pseudonymized sample you provide. Also let us know if HIPAA BAAs are required — we will route this to legal.

I'll prepare a short runnable notebook and a reproducible metrics overview. Rishi/Monica: I'll need a slot with your calendars for the tech sync tomorrow morning.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Applied ML, Redwood Inference
